description:
ERDEMLİ GELECEK, bilim, teknoloji, mühendislik ve yazılım alanlarına ilgi duyan, üretmeyi ve birlikte öğrenmeyi hedefleyen bir ekiptir. Süleyman Erdeğer liderliğinde Taha Özçelik, Muhammed Emir Gezgin, Barış Çekirge ve Tarık Tuna Yıldız'dan oluşuyoruz.

Robotik kodlama, STEM, elektronik alanlarındaki ilgimizi uzay teknolojileriyle birleştirerek yenilikçi projeler geliştirmeyi amaçlıyoruz. NASA Space Apps Challenge kapsamında etkileşimli bir Uzay Görevi Tasarım Oyunu geliştirmeyi hedefliyoruz.
summary:
As the ERDEMLİ GELECEK team, we developed an interactive Space Mission Design Simulation Game that enables students and space enthusiasts to design, manage, and simulate interplanetary missions under real-world engineering constraints.

For learners without access to hands-on mission operations, competing engineering trade-offs—such as budget limits, payload mass capacity, Delta-V requirements, and energy balance—often remain abstract. Our game addresses this challenge by letting players select launch vehicles, power systems (solar panels vs. nuclear MMRTGs), and scientific instruments for targets like the Moon, Mars, or Europa. During live simulation, players experience real physics—including the inverse-square law—and make autonomous strategic decisions against space weather crises like solar flares and radiation belts.

This project matters because it transforms complex aerospace systems engineering into an accessible, engaging learning tool that builds critical STEM problem-solving skills
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Developed by ERDEMLİ GELECEK, the Space Mission Design & Simulation Center is an interactive, browser-based aerospace engineering simulator where players step into the role of a Lead Mission Architect. The experience unfolds in three structured phases:

  1. Mission Scoping & Target Selection: Players select a real interplanetary destination—the Moon (South Pole), Mars, or Jupiter's moon Europa—each defined by authentic distance, communication latency, solar irradiance, radiation levels, and Delta-V requirements.
  2. Spacecraft Engineering & Trade-Offs: Within strict budget and mass limits, players configure four core subsystems: Launch Vehicles (light, medium, or heavy class), Power Systems (compact/wide solar arrays vs. nuclear MMRTG), Communications & Radiation Shielding, and multi-select Scientific Payloads (High-Res Camera, Mass Spectrometer, Subsurface Ice Radar, Laser Magnetometer). As components are selected, a live dynamic CAD schematic (SVG) updates the spacecraft's visual configuration in real time while telemetry bars calculate budget, mass, net power balance, and effective Delta-V.
  3. Live Hohmann Transfer Simulation & Crisis Management: Once launched, an animated Hohmann transfer trajectory tracks the spacecraft's journey. Along the way, real-time space weather and operational crises—such as X-Class Solar Flares (DONKI alerts), Jupiter's magnetospheric radiation belts, Martian dust storms, and cryogenic thermal drops—pause the simulation and require players to make strategic trade-off decisions (e.g., entering Safe Mode vs. pushing data collection). Finally, a Post-Mortem STEM Root-Cause Analysis evaluates their engineering choices.

Benefits & Intended Impact Space systems engineering often feels abstract to students because they rarely get to experience how changing one subsystem affects the entire mission. Our simulator makes complex physics tangible by allowing students to fail safely, iterate on their designs, and immediately observe cause-and-effect relationships. Because it runs directly in any web browser with zero installation, it serves as an accessible, ready-to-use educational tool for STEM classrooms, robotics clubs, and aspiring young engineers worldwide.

Tools, Coding Languages & Technologies Used

  • Core Languages: HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+) for real-time telemetry state management, physics calculations, and simulation loops.
  • Styling & UI: Tailwind CSS, Google Fonts (Inter & JetBrains Mono), and Font Awesome for a dark-mode NASA Mission Control interface.
  • Graphics & Audio: Custom dynamic SVG generation for live spacecraft CAD assembly, HTML5 Canvas API for animated Hohmann transfer trajectories, and Tone.js for procedural sci-fi telemetry audio cues.
  • Hosting & Version Control: GitHub and GitHub Pages for open-source code hosting and instant public web deployment.

Creativity & Key Engineering Factors Considered Rather than building a traditional arcade space game, our team focused on authentic physical constraints and educational storytelling:

  • The Inverse-Square Law: Solar panel efficiency scales realistically with distance from the Sun (100% at the Moon, 43% at Mars, and just 4% at Europa). Players who attempt an Europa mission without an MMRTG experience real power starvation and thermal freezing, intuitively learning why deep-space missions require radioisotope power.
  • Mass-to-Delta-V Coupling: Adding heavier instruments or thick tantalum/polyethylene radiation armor directly reduces the rocket's effective Delta-V, forcing realistic compromises between scientific capability, survivability, and launch cost.
  • Built-in STEM Engineering Guide: We integrated an interactive reference guide and post-mission diagnostics so every playthrough reinforces core aerospace principles.
